metadata.case_name: LAI YEE KIN v. TOP-CROWN ELECTROPLATING FACTORY LTD.

plaintiff.occupation_before: metal worker / skilled or semi-skilled manual worker
plaintiff.occupation_after: casual worker; acupuncturist's assistant; quality controller in a Shenzen factory

injuries.description: Crushing injuries to the left hand with traumatic amputation of parts of four fingers; loss of terminal phalanx of the index finger and of the terminal and middle phalanges of the remaining fingers; thumb intact; treated by revision amputations of all fingers and closure of stumps.
source: The plaintiff claims damages for injuries to his left hand which was crushed in a power press during his employment by defendant. As a result of the accident parts of four fingers were amputated.

The initial admission report from the United Christian Hospital revealed crushing injuries to the left hand. The index finger suffered loss of pulp and the other three fingers traumatic amputations. The treatment was by way of revision amputations of all fingers and closure of stumps. This report was dated 26th October 1983 and was produced as Exhibit P. 3.

In regard to the injuries the doctor noted the loss of the terminal phalanx of the index finger and of the terminal and middle phalanges of the remaining fingers. The thumb was intact. There was good soft tissue cover over the amputations and discomfort was felt only if the stumps were bent acutely forward.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified traumatic amputation of two or more fingers alone

manifestations.description: Considerable pain at the time of the accident (required an anaesthetic injection once in hospital when he was in pain).
Residual pain in the injured hand in cold weather; only occasionally needed treatment for this.
Reduced grip strength: 38 pound grip with the injured hand as apposed to 60 pounds with the right hand.
Poor handwriting with the other hand (injured hand was the plaintiff's preferred hand and handwriting with the other hand was of 'very poor quality').

Loss of the terminal phalanx of the index finger and of the terminal and middle phalanges of the remaining fingers with wholeman impairment assessed at 20% (index finger 45% giving 6% wholeman; middle, ring and fifth fingers 80% giving 8%, 4% and 2% wholeman respectively).
Deterioration in recreational and social lifestyle; deprived of regular enjoyment of table tennis and badminton.
Cosmetic disability and plaintiff's awareness of the effect of this on others.
Diminished prospects of marriage (relationship with a former girl-friend stopped as she claimed his injury would prevent his working after marriage).

treatments_received: revision amputations of all fingers and closure of stumps

losses.description: Mutilation and amputation of parts of four fingers of the left hand with permanent impairment and reduced grip strength.
Cosmetic disability and plaintiff's awareness of the effect of this on others.

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: Deprived of regular enjoyment of table tennis and badminton.
Diminished prospects of marriage illustrated by the ending of a relationship because the girl considered his injury would prevent his working after marriage.

Uncertainty in working life and reduced ability to compete for employment due to loss of normal hand function; likelihood of reduced employment prospects as many employers prefer a man with two normal hands.

comparable_cases.injury_description: Facts very similar to the present case, though injuries were less serious; earnings related disability assessed at 22 - 25%.
Hand injury similar in nature but considerably less serious: two fingers fractured, one other partly amputated; wholeman impairment assessed at 10%.
Injuries of a broadly similar nature; award of $75,000 in April 1984 (noted that updating for inflation would give a figure in excess of $100,000).
